key_insight: Homogeneous WC–Co–Cr powder enables dense cermet coatings, while spray method mainly tunes the balance between hardness and tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical machine parts, choosing between DS and HVOF lets engineers optimize either maximum hardness or lower friction and higher coating density.
method: Compare WC–Co–Cr coatings made by detonation spray (DS) and HVOF.
Characterize powder morphology, coating microstructure, and phase composition using SEM and EDS.
Evaluate mechanical and tribological performance via microhardness and friction behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a harder DS coating with average microhardness of 1449 HV, while HVOF produced a dense, uniform coating with a low friction coefficient (Kt = 0.143).
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on powder morphology and spray parameters, so results may not transfer directly without matching feedstock quality and process conditions.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
